statement: Measured on synthetic data with planted signals: Fjordvik Manufacturing Oy is fictional, and these are not results on real pumps or a real service team.
what_a_score_means: the model's estimate of the chance that this pump has a failure in the 30 days after this day, from readings up to the end of this day
ceiling: some failures give no warning, so no model can catch them; every result shows that share (W8)
outside_the_grid: library defaults, listed under params, including early stopping on a held-out 10% of training rows

threshold_rule.rule: M3: chosen on validation only, from the costs, using failures from fact_service_event and no answer key, so it can run on live data
threshold_rule.criterion: lowest cost of the model plan over the validation alert window at the central missed-failure cost, counting every failure as preventable
threshold_rule.candidates: every distinct score on the validation at-risk rows in the alert window
threshold_rule.ties: ties go to fewer visits; if still tied, the higher threshold
threshold_rule.stored: with the model version, in eval/ml/split_lock.json and the model card; the test step refuses a threshold from another version; chosen again after every retrain

data_handling: A day with no running has no reading: its power of zero is treated as blank.
Fleet-adjusted readings are rounded to 9 decimal places before the baseline spread is taken, removing floating-point noise; every sensor is recorded to 0.1 or 0.01 of its unit.
A robust z-score with a zero baseline spread, or fewer than 60 baseline readings, is blank.
The isolation forest reads a blank input as 0, no change from the baseline.
Used alone, the robust z-score ranks rows with no z-score lowest.
random_generators: numpy RandomState(PCG64(seed)), made fresh for each fit (G10)
